definitions.explanation: A set phrase said to someone who has just returned home or to a place. It is the standard response to ただいま.

examples.japanese: 「ただいま」「お{帰|かえ}りなさい」
お{帰|かえ}りなさい。{疲|つか}れたでしょう？
examples.english: Welcome back. You must be tired.

examples.japanese: お{帰|かえ}りなさい。{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}かったですね。
{子|こ}どもたちが「お{帰|かえ}りなさい」と{言|い}って{玄関|げんかん}まで{走|はし}ってきました。
examples.english: The children said "welcome back" and ran to the entrance.

notes:
お{帰|かえ}りなさい is the standard greeting said to someone returning home, functioning as the response to ただいま.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- お{帰|かえ}り: casual (family, close friends)
- お{帰|かえ}りなさい: polite (standard)
- お{帰|かえ}りなさいませ: very formal (hotel/shop staff)

USAGE:
This exchange is a daily ritual in Japanese households:
- Returning person: 「ただいま」
- Person at home: 「お{帰|かえ}りなさい」

CULTURE:
The phrase literally means "please return" (from {帰|かえ}る). It welcomes someone back to a shared space, whether home, office, or other regular location. Some workplaces also use this greeting when colleagues return from outside meetings.
